surface_mechanism_description: The surface reactions during ALD involve the adsorption of TaCl5 and H2O on the substrate, leading to the formation of tantalum oxide films. The mechanism includes the adsorption of TaCl5, followed by the reaction with surface hydroxyl groups, and subsequent purging. The presence of residual chlorine and the role of surface reactions in forming suboxides and crystalline phases are discussed.
evidence: The text discusses the adsorption of TaCl5 and H2O on the substrate, the formation of surface hydroxyl groups, and the role of residual chlorine in the film structure. It also mentions the formation of suboxides (TaOx) and their influence on the optical properties of the films.
